correctness.rationale: The roots of P_m are simple nonidentity m-th roots of unity. For a common root z of P_m(X),P_m(X+h), the two unit-modulus equations give Re z=−h/2. For h>2 this is impossible; h=2 translates the only candidate −1 to the excluded root 1. For h=1 the candidates have orders 3 and their translates have order 6, giving exactly the quadratic factor precisely when 6 divides m. After exact monic division, the residual evaluated GCD equals gcd(A(b),B(b),C) where C is the absolute nonzero resultant, giving divisibility, periodicity and the growth dichotomy. Independently expanding the original polynomials in ZZ verified the length-six bound after parity and the length-twelve resultant 1023252616422400. At length twelve there is no common root modulo 2; the listed roots modulo 5,7,13 have exactly the displayed disjoint lift digits modulo the respective squares. Hence the residual is squarefree. CRT gives the eight values and their frequencies; any period has to preserve each nonconstant prime indicator, forcing divisibility by all three primes. The independent replay also rejected all smaller cyclic shifts of the exact evaluated table.
residual_risks: Growth and bounded periodicity are for fixed m and h. Complete spectra are proved only for h=1 and lengths 6 and 12. The length-six Bézout constant 14 is not its resultant, which the independent replay found to be 196.

evidence: Frenkel–Pelikán explicitly give the resultant bound and a period for monic integral polynomials. Bodin–Dèbes–Najib establish finiteness and periodicity in one variable. The several-variable theorem is about stability under gcd and lcm. Komatsu's shifted geometric question is additive representation, not a GCD comparison.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The univariate abstract results already cover the bounded residual once the common factor is known; they do not identify the possible common complex roots or resolve the valuations when the resultant is not squarefree.

evidence: P_m is the product of cyclotomics with nonidentity orders dividing m. A translated factor is not generally an untranslated cyclotomic. The actual third-cyclotomic record takes only Phi_3 at its two or more shifted inputs.

originality.rationale: The general divisibility and periodicity theorem for coprime polynomial values is established prior work, and the finding does not claim it as new. The supported distinctions are the classification of which equal-length shifted repunit pairs have a common polynomial factor, and the exact two exceptional-length residual laws, in particular the length-twelve local square obstructions and least period. None of the inspected table comparators has these two polynomial inputs. The citation summary in RESULT.md line 99 overgroups Bodin–Dèbes (arXiv:2105.13883) with the univariate periodicity sources: its several-variable theorem concerns gcd/lcm stability and permits infinite sets. This is a literature-description correction, not a flaw in the theorem, whose periodicity proof is self-contained and also matches the separate univariate references.
residual_risks: Unavailable full text by Ruiz and an indexed snippet on unshifted cyclotomic resultants were not used to exclude prior coverage. Unindexed equal-length GCD tables remain possible. No relative priority is inferred from the two distinct same-day records.

value.rationale: Fixing the length and varying the positive base gap is a natural classification of shared divisibility across repunit bases. The unique quadratic-growth family and the two exact initial exceptional spectra give mathematically meaningful boundary data; the length-twelve example separates the coarse resultant bound from sharp simultaneous prime-power divisibility and from the true period.
residual_risks: No closed exact spectrum is established for later exceptional lengths.
